reading.text:
Unit: def:LevyStochCalc.Driver.sigmaPoisson (reading locked before any Lean is seen)

Paper notion. The sigma-field generated by the Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E (Section 2,
lines 224-228), used for "W and an independent Poisson random measure N" and for the generated
filtration: sigma(N) = sigma(N(A) : A in B(R_+) (x) E), or its time-t version
sigma(N(A) : A in B([0,t]) (x) E).

What a faithful Lean definition must be.
- The sigma-algebra on Omega generated by the random variables omega |-> N(omega)(A), A measurable in
  (time) x E (supremum of comap of N(A) with the Borel sigma-algebra on R>=0oo / N u {oo}); if
  time-indexed, A restricted to [0,t] x E (or (0,t] x E). Generating only by finite-intensity A gives
  the same sigma-algebra (sigma-finiteness). Generating by the measure-valued map omega |-> N(omega)
  with the standard (Giry) sigma-algebra on measures is also the same sigma-algebra.
- Raw (no null sets). If not time-indexed, it must be the whole sigma(N) (for independence statements).

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Driver.sigmaPoisson
(Driver/Joint.lean:31-33.)

- Reading: sigma(N) = sigma(N(A) : A measurable in time x E), the whole sigma(N) when not time-indexed;
  raw; generating by finite-intensity sets or by the measure-valued map gives the same.
- Lean: sup over measurable B subset R x E of comap (omega |-> N.N omega B) (Borel of R>=0oo). Exactly the
  sigma-algebra generated by all counts; raw; <= ambient (sigmaPoisson_le). Negative-time counts are a.s. 0
  and add only P-trivial events.

Verdict: faithful.
